title: Hanson–Wright inequality
statement: ℙ(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp[−c min{t²/V, t/L}], for every real A and t ≥ 0.
original_proof:
Proof. Write Q = XᵀAX − 𝔼XᵀAX, K = maxᵢ ‖Xᵢ‖ψ₂, V = K⁴‖A‖F², and L = K²‖A‖. If A = 0 or K = 0, then Q = 0 almost surely, so the result is immediate; the case t = 0 is also immediate. Henceforth assume t > 0 and V,L > 0. Constants c,C > 0 below are absolute and may change from line to line.

It suffices to bound ℙ(Q ≥ t). Indeed, replacing A by −A replaces Q by −Q and preserves both matrix norms. The same upper-tail estimate therefore applies to the lower tail, and the two estimates can be combined by the union bound.

By independence and the mean-zero assumption, 𝔼(XᵢXⱼ) = 0 for i ≠ j. Consequently, Q = ∑ᵢ aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²) + ∑ᵢ≠ⱼ aᵢⱼXᵢXⱼ =: D + S.

We estimate the two sums separately. Since D + S ≥ t implies that D ≥ t/2 or S ≥ t/2, ℙ(Q ≥ t) ≤ ℙ(D ≥ t/2) + ℙ(S ≥ t/2). No independence between D and S is required for this reduction.

The variables Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ² are independent, centered, and subexponential, with ‖Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²‖ψ₁ ≤ CK². Bernstein’s inequality, together with ∑ᵢ aᵢᵢ² ≤ ‖A‖F² and maxᵢ |aᵢᵢ| ≤ ‖A‖, yields ℙ(D ≥ t/2) ≤ exp[−c min{t²/V, t/L}]. If the diagonal of A is zero, this estimate holds directly because D = 0.

For the off-diagonal sum, fix λ > 0. Applying Markov’s inequality to exp(λS), we obtain ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/2) 𝔼 exp(λS). We will prove that 𝔼 exp(λS) ≤ exp(CVλ²) for 0 < λ ≤ c₀/L, and then choose λ in that range.

Let X′ be an independent copy of X. The off-diagonal decoupling inequality, applied to the convex function s ↦ exp(λs), gives 𝔼 exp(λS) ≤ 𝔼 exp(4λXᵀAX′). The version used here permits the full matrix A on the right. Conditional on X′, the bilinear form XᵀAX′ is the linear form ⟨X,AX′⟩ with fixed coefficients.

For every fixed vector v and every real η, independence and the mean-zero subgaussian MGF estimate imply 𝔼 exp(η⟨X,v⟩) = ∏ᵢ 𝔼 exp(ηvᵢXᵢ) ≤ ∏ᵢ exp(CK²η²vᵢ²) = exp(CK²η²‖v‖₂²).

Let g,g′ be independent standard Gaussian vectors, independent of X,X′. The Gaussian MGF identity is 𝔼g exp(μ⟨g,v⟩) = exp(μ²‖v‖₂²/2). Choosing μ = √(2C)Kη matches the preceding subgaussian upper bound. Condition first on X′ and use v = AX′ to replace X by g. Average over X′, then condition on g and apply the same argument to X′. Absorbing the decoupling factor 4 into an absolute constant, we obtain 𝔼 exp(4λXᵀAX′) ≤ 𝔼 exp(C₁K²λgᵀAg′).

Write A = U diag(sᵢ)Rᵀ. By Gaussian rotation invariance, Uᵀg and Rᵀg′ remain independent standard Gaussian vectors. Therefore gᵀAg′ has the same distribution as ∑ᵢ sᵢgᵢgᵢ′, and independence of the pairs gives 𝔼 exp(θgᵀAg′) = ∏ᵢ 𝔼 exp(θsᵢgᵢgᵢ′).

For independent scalar standard Gaussians g₁,g₁′, conditioning on g₁ and then using the MGF of g₁² gives 𝔼 exp(ug₁g₁′) = 𝔼 exp(u²g₁²/2) = (1 − u²)−1/2 ≤ exp(u²), u² ≤ 1/2. Here the inequality follows from −½ log(1−z) ≤ z for 0 ≤ z ≤ 1/2. Substituting u = θsᵢ in each factor, and using ∑ᵢsᵢ² = ‖A‖F² and maxᵢsᵢ = ‖A‖, yields 𝔼 exp(θgᵀAg′) ≤ exp(θ²‖A‖F²), |θ| ≤ 1/(√2 ‖A‖).

Combining decoupling, replacement, and the Gaussian estimate with θ = C₁K²λ proves 𝔼 exp(λS) ≤ exp(CK⁴λ²‖A‖F²) = exp(CVλ²), |λ| ≤ c₀/L. The absolute constant c₀ accounts for the parameter rescaling. This is the exponential-moment estimate required above.

The exponential Markov bound now becomes ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/2 + CVλ²). Choose λ = min{t/(4CV), c₀/(2L)}. This choice is admissible and satisfies CVλ² ≤ λt/4. It follows that ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/4) ≤ exp[−c min{t²/V, t/L}].

Combining the bounds for D and S gives the upper-tail estimate for Q. Apply the same argument to −A and add the two tail probabilities. With q = min{t²/V,t/L}, this gives ℙ(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ min{1, 4 exp(−cq)} ≤ 2 exp(−cq/2). Indeed, when q ≤ 2 log(2)/c the last expression is at least 1; otherwise it bounds 4 exp(−cq). Renaming c/2 as c establishes the stated inequality. □

# First-move ablation: the upper-tail reduction

## Protocol fixed before model results

Remove reference action `sign`, from `state:start`: the reduction of the two-sided
Hanson–Wright goal to an upper-tail bound, followed by applying it to −A.
The proposed pilot starts from the theorem and assumptions and prohibits this
strategy throughout the argument, including signed-tail/cosh disguises. It permits
absolute moments, independent copies, conditioning and lower-level scalar/linear
and independent-sum toolkit results. The complete machine-readable restriction
and prompts are in `tools/proof_explorer/ablation_study.py`.

Two fresh attempts per condition (unrestricted and restricted); model configured
by the existing project; medium reasoning; 6,500 completion-token cap per search
call; at most two search calls per trial. A separate review call has a 4,500 cap.
One revision after review is allowed. Stop on acceptance; at most 16 calls across
all trials. Review is by the same model in a separate context, not formal checking.
No reference proof, other trial, or the local derivation below enters the requests.
Full requests, public responses, provider token usage and call duration are logged.
Review costs are separated from search costs. A failed finite budget is censored,
not infinite difficulty. This is a small descriptive pilot, not a statistical
criticality estimate or an incremental student/professor run.

The API usage fields and completion-token limit follow the
[official API documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create).
The completion cap includes reasoning tokens as well as visible output.

## Local mathematical reconstruction, separate from the empirical pilot

This derivation was constructed by the coding assistant while API execution was
awaiting approval. It is not a fresh model-search sample, has no measured search
cost, and must not be counted in the empirical success rate.

There is a route around the sign reduction: prove an absolute-moment estimate and
apply Markov directly to |Q|ᵖ. No upper-tail theorem for Q or −Q is needed.

Write F=‖A‖F, O=‖A‖ and Q=D+S, where

    D = Σᵢ aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ²−E Xᵢ²),    S = Σᵢ≠ⱼ aᵢⱼ Xᵢ Xⱼ.

For even p≥2, the independent centered subexponential-sum moment inequality gives

    ‖D‖p ≤ C K²(√p F + p O).

Toolkit dependency: for independent centered subexponential Yi and fixed weights
bi, ‖Σ bi Yi‖p ≤ C(√p (Σ bi²‖Yi‖ψ₁²)¹ᐟ² + p max |bi|‖Yi‖ψ₁).
Here Yi=Xi²−E Xi² has ψ₁ norm at most CK². The inequalities
Σ aᵢᵢ²≤F² and max|aᵢᵢ|≤O check the required scales. This is an
independent-sum moment result, not a quadratic-form concentration theorem.

To check that this does not conceal a signed-tail reduction, it can be proved
directly by expanding even powers. Set Zi=aᵢᵢYi, choose Mi=C K²|aᵢᵢ| so that
E|Zi|ᵏ≤k! Miᵏ for k≥2, and put σ²=ΣMi², b=max Mi. Centering removes terms
with exponent one. Independence and the multinomial expansion give the following
coefficient-wise bound of formal power series, for p=2m:

    E|Σ Zi|²ᵐ / (2m)! ≤ [z²ᵐ] ∏ᵢ (1 + Σₖ≥₂ Miᵏ zᵏ)
                       ≤ [z²ᵐ] exp(σ²z²/(1−bz)).

All coefficients in the upper bound are nonnegative. For any 0<r<1/b, the last
coefficient is at most r⁻²ᵐ exp(σ²r²/(1−br)). Take
r=min{√m/(2σ),1/(2b)}. The exponent is at most m/2, and (2m)!¹ᐟ²ᵐ≤2m.
Thus ‖ΣZi‖₂ₘ≤C(√m σ+mb), as needed. Zero coefficients give the immediate
degenerate case. This uses coefficient estimates for even moments, not a tail
estimate for D or −D; it introduces no signed quadratic-form MGF.

Let δi be independent Bernoulli(1/2) selectors, independent of X, and define
Sδ=Σᵢ≠ⱼ δi(1−δj)aᵢⱼXiXj. Since Eδ Sδ=S/4, Jensen gives

    ‖S‖p ≤ 4(Eδ E|Sδ|ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ.

For fixed Λ={i:δi=1}, Sδ=XΛᵀB XΛᶜ with B=AΛ,Λᶜ. The two vectors are
independent, even for nonsymmetric A. Conditional scalar linear-form moments yield

    ‖Sδ‖p ≤ CK√p · (E‖B XΛᶜ‖₂ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ.

The necessary vector bound follows without a signed quadratic MGF. Let g be an
independent standard Gaussian vector in the output space of B and ap=‖g₁‖p≈√p. Gaussian
projection followed by conditioning on g gives

    ap (E‖BY‖₂ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ = (E|⟨g,BY⟩|ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ
                          ≤ CK√p (E‖Bᵀg‖₂ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ.

The standard Gaussian Lipschitz moment inequality implies

    (E‖Bᵀg‖₂ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ ≤ E‖Bᵀg‖₂ + C√p‖B‖
                       ≤ ‖B‖F + C√p‖B‖.

This follows from Theorem 5.2.3 (Gaussian concentration) and the subgaussian
moment characterization in Proposition 2.6.1 of the supplied HDP-2 book.
Its hypotheses hold because g is standard Gaussian and g↦‖Bᵀg‖₂ is
‖B‖-Lipschitz. Jensen bounds its mean by ‖B‖F. This is a Gaussian Lipschitz
toolkit dependency, not Hanson–Wright in disguise. Dividing by ap yields

    (E‖BY‖₂ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ ≤ CK(‖B‖F + √p‖B‖).

Coordinate projections give ‖B‖F≤F and ‖B‖≤O, so

    ‖S‖p ≤ CK²(√p F + p O),
    ‖Q‖p ≤ C₀K²(√p F + p O).

For q=min{t²/(K⁴F²),t/(K²O)}, choose a universal α>0 with
C₀(√α+α)≤1/e. If αq≥4, take the even integer p=2⌊αq/2⌋.
Then αq/2≤p≤αq. Apply Markov directly:

    P(|Q|≥t) ≤ (‖Q‖p/t)ᵖ ≤ exp(−p) ≤ exp(−αq/2).

For αq<4 use P≤1. Taking c≤α log(2)/4 gives the requested uniform bound
P(|Q|≥t)≤2exp(−cq) in both regimes. At t=0 the bound is immediate. If A=0
or K=0, Q=0 almost surely and positive-threshold probabilities vanish.

### What this establishes and what it does not

The sign/upper-tail reduction is mathematically replaceable relative to the
stated toolkit. The replacement route bypasses the upper-tail checkpoint and
reaches the final two-sided theorem directly. It carries additional explicit
moment and Gaussian-Lipschitz dependencies. This derivation alone says nothing
about how easily a fresh search finds the route, how much it costs relative to a
baseline, or whether the first move is empirically critical for a given model.

# Step 2 — `expand`: separate diagonal and off-diagonal terms

## Original move and global restriction

The original move writes Q = D + S, using independence and centering to remove
cross terms from E XᵀAX. It exposes an independent sum of squares and a dependent
cross-term sum.

For a meaningful structural ablation, forbid this diagonal/off-diagonal
separation **anywhere in the new proof**, including hollow-matrix notation,
separate lemmas for those two contributions, or a coordinate induction that
quietly analyzes precisely the same two pieces. Do not prohibit algebra or the
use of independence itself. Those would be much broader restrictions.

The existing moment proof is inadmissible: its first substantive operation is
exactly Q = D + S.

## Alternative tried analytically: whole-form symmetrization

Replace A by B = (A + Aᵀ)/2. This preserves the quadratic form and gives
‖B‖ ≤ O and ‖B‖F ≤ F without separating the diagonal. Let X′ be an independent
copy. Conditional Jensen and polarization yield, for p ≥ 2,

    ‖Q‖p ≤ ‖XᵀBX − X′ᵀBX′‖p
          = ‖(X − X′)ᵀB(X + X′)‖p.

This is a valid change of representation under the stated ban. A direct
Cauchy–Schwarz bound gives

    ‖Q‖p ≤ O · ‖X − X′‖L₂ₚ(ℓ₂) · ‖X + X′‖L₂ₚ(ℓ₂)
          ≤ CK² O(n + p).

The last inequality uses the vector norm moment bound from the first-step note,
applied to the identity matrix. It follows from scalar linear-form moments and
Gaussian projection/Lipschitz control; it does not use a D/S split of Q.

## Why this does not close the required theorem

The target moment scale is K²(√p F + p O). For A = I, the displayed alternative
has order K²(n+p), whereas the target is K²(√pn+p). At fixed p and growing n,
the available bound is too coarse. This is a loss in the **proved bound**, not a
measurement of computational cost or a proof that every polarized route fails.

A tempting next line treats X − X′ and X + X′ as independent. That is false for
general subgaussian coordinates. For independent Rademacher Xᵢ,Xᵢ′, their sum
and difference multiply to zero, and each is nonzero with positive probability;
they are not independent. Independence holds in the Gaussian special case, which
is not enough for the stated theorem.

An admissible continuation would need a sharp bound for this dependent bilinear
expression without reintroducing diagonal/off-diagonal separation. That bound
has not been supplied here. Calling Hanson–Wright for it would be circular.

## Graph representation, cost, and conclusion

    original assumptions
      → symmetrize the matrix
      → independent-copy centering and polarization
      → dependent bilinear moment obligation
      → coarse O(n+p) estimate / sharp continuation unresolved

There is no justified rejoin or theorem closure. Record the coarse candidate as
**insufficient for the required norm scales**, with the broader ablation
**unresolved**. It is not an infinite-difficulty branch. A restriction against
only the literal coordinate expansion, while allowing the same D/S decomposition
under different notation, would test presentation rather than this strategy.

Search cost and historical frequency are unmeasured. See the [shared protocol](00-common.md).

# Step 3 — `split`: allocate t/2 to two tail events

## Original move and global restriction

The original edge bounds P(D+S ≥ t) by P(D ≥ t/2)+P(S ≥ t/2). Here the ablated
strategy is **splitting a deviation event into diagonal and off-diagonal tail
events and allocating thresholds to them**, including unequal allocations.
Ban that operation throughout the proof.

Algebraically writing Q = D + S remains allowed. This makes the experiment
distinct from the stronger structural ban in [step 2](02-expand.md). If “give
the terms different jobs” is intended to prohibit *any* separate treatment of D
and S, the alternative below is inadmissible and step 2's unresolved conclusion
applies instead. This scope must be fixed before a search trial.

## Worked alternative: combine transforms before taking a tail

Start again from the theorem. Establish the diagonal MGF by calculation E in
[the shared notes](00-common.md). Establish the off-diagonal MGF through the
permitted decoupling, Gaussian replacement and Gaussian computation route:

    E exp(uD) ≤ exp(C_D V u²), |u| ≤ a_D/L,
    E exp(uS) ≤ exp(C_S V u²), |u| ≤ a_S/L.

For negative u use the same permitted estimates with −A. Now apply
Cauchy–Schwarz, not a decomposition of the tail event:

    E exp(λQ) ≤ √(E exp(2λD) E exp(2λS))
               ≤ exp(2(C_D+C_S)Vλ²),
    |λ| ≤ min(a_D,a_S)/(2L).

Calculation H in the shared notes then gives the complete two-sided theorem.
D and S need not be independent. The domain shrinkage by 2 is part of the
argument, not a dispensable constant annotation.

A second admissible route is the [absolute-moment proof](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md):
combine D and S by Minkowski and apply Markov to |Q|ᵖ. It also avoids splitting
the D/S tail event, but still treats the algebraic pieces separately.

## Other natural attempt and its failure

Writing E exp(λ(D+S)) = E exp(λD) E exp(λS) would be shorter, but D and S share
coordinates. No such independence is assumed. The Schwarz inequality above is
what makes the transformed assembly valid without that false factorization.

## Rejoin and implications

    assumptions → D/S MGF estimates → whole-Q MGF
                → whole-Q Chernoff bound → two-sided theorem

The route bypasses the two tail checkpoints. It reaches the original endpoint,
rather than pretending to recreate the old `split` state. The existing diagonal
tail result alone is not enough for the Schwarz step; the diagonal MGF must be
proved explicitly.

**Conclusion:** worked replacement under the event-splitting ban. Constants
change but the Frobenius/operator norm scales are retained. No discovery-cost
comparison is available. This does not show that the stronger diagonal/off-diagonal
structural split is replaceable.

# Step 4 — `bernstein`: close the diagonal with an exponential sum bound

## Original move and global restriction

The original proof applies Bernstein to independent centered subexponential
summands Zᵢ = aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ² − EXᵢ²).

Ban invoking Bernstein for this diagonal sum **and** reconstructing its usual
exponential-MGF/Chernoff proof for D under another name. Permit even-power moment
calculations and absolute Markov. A ban on the resulting two-scale inequality
itself would forbid a necessary special case of the target theorem when A is
diagonal, so it would not isolate a proof technique.

## Worked alternative: positive coefficient estimates

The complete calculation is in the [first-step note](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md).
Its relevant steps are reproduced here to make the replacement explicit.
Choose Mᵢ = CK²|aᵢᵢ| with E|Zᵢ|ᵏ ≤ k!Mᵢᵏ for k ≥ 2, and set
σ² = ΣMᵢ², b = max Mᵢ. Centering kills singleton factors in an even-power expansion:

    E|ΣZᵢ|²ᵐ/(2m)!
      ≤ [z²ᵐ] ∏ᵢ(1 + Σₖ≥₂ Mᵢᵏzᵏ)
      ≤ [z²ᵐ] exp(σ²z²/(1−bz)).

This is a coefficientwise majorant of a formal series, not E exp(λD). Its
coefficients are nonnegative. Evaluate at

    r = min{√m/(2σ), 1/(2b)}.

The coefficient is at most r⁻²ᵐ exp(m/2), and ((2m)!)¹ᐟ²ᵐ ≤ 2m. Thus

    ‖D‖₂ₘ ≤ C(√m σ + mb) ≤ CK²(√p F + p O), p = 2m.

If b = 0, D = 0 and no radius is needed. Follow the existing off-diagonal moment
route, use Minkowski, and close the full theorem by the even-order Markov
argument M in [the shared notes](00-common.md). No diagonal exponential tail or
MGF has been used.

## A cheaper-looking attempt that loses the theorem's scale

Triangle inequality term by term gives

    ‖D‖p ≤ Σᵢ |aᵢᵢ| ‖Xᵢ²−EXᵢ²‖p
          ≤ CK²p Σᵢ|aᵢᵢ|.

For A = I this is CK²pn rather than CK²(√pn+p). It discards the cancellation
from centering. The coefficient argument retains that cancellation through the
absence of exponent-one terms.

## Rejoin, cost, and conclusion

The preferred branch reaches the diagonal **moment** goal, then the full moment
goal and final theorem. It does not directly rejoin the original diagonal-tail
state unless a separate moment-to-tail inference is included.

**Conclusion:** worked replacement for the specified exponential independent-sum
strategy. It adds coefficient bookkeeping and an even-moment parameter choice.
That extra mathematical work is visible, but its discovery cost is unmeasured.
If the ban is broadened to all centered independent-sum moment aggregation, this
argument no longer qualifies; it should not be counted under that broader ban.

# Step 5 — `exponential`: turn a quadratic tail into an MGF goal

## Original move and global restriction

The reference proof applies exponential Markov to S and asks for
E exp(λS) ≤ exp(CVλ²) on a cutoff interval.

Ban the entire quadratic-MGF/Chernoff strategy for Q, D, S and their transformed
quadratic or bilinear substitutes. This includes cosh or signed-MGF disguises
and quoting a quadratic MGF lemma that performs the omitted work internally.
Scalar/linear subgaussian toolkit results and Gaussian norm concentration remain
available; an auxiliary norm's Lipschitz concentration is not a quadratic-form
MGF bound.

## Worked alternative: control |Q| by its even moments

Use the [first-step moment construction](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md),
with its dependencies explicitly retained:

    Q = D + S;
    ‖D‖p ≤ CK²(√p F + p O)              [even-power coefficients];
    ‖S‖p ≤ CK²(√p F + p O)              [selectors and vector moments];
    ‖Q‖p ≤ C₀K²(√p F + p O)            [Minkowski].

The off-diagonal estimate follows from

    ‖S‖p ≤ 4‖XΛᵀB XΛᶜ‖Lp(δ,X),
    ‖XΛᵀB Y‖p ≤ CK√p ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂),
    ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ CK(‖B‖F + √p‖B‖).

The last line uses a Gaussian projection and the Lipschitz moment bound for
‖Bᵀg‖₂, not a Gaussian bilinear MGF. Uniform bounds ‖B‖F ≤ F and ‖B‖ ≤ O
allow averaging over the selectors. The diagonal's formal coefficient majorant
is likewise not a random quadratic exponential moment.

Apply Markov to |Q|ᵖ with the even p and small-q handling specified in calculation
M of [the shared notes](00-common.md). This reaches the full two-sided theorem.

## Why second moments alone do not replace Chernoff

At p = 2 the construction gives E Q² ≤ CK⁴F²: O ≤ F absorbs the second term.
Chebyshev then gives only P(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ CK⁴F²/t². This is a valid polynomial tail,
but it does not establish the required exponential tail. A family of increasing
moment orders is doing essential work in the successful replacement.

## Graph, cost, and conclusion

    quadratic tail goal → all-even-moment goal
       → diagonal/off-diagonal moment branches → full moment bound
       → absolute Markov with even rounding → theorem

The route bypasses the original MGF checkpoint completely. It must not be drawn
as having established that checkpoint along the way.

**Conclusion:** worked replacement. It is the same substantive alternative as
the first-step construction, admissible under a different ban; it is not a new
independent search success. Search cost, probability of rediscovery, and any
relative advantage over the MGF route remain unmeasured.

# Step 7 — `decouple`: replace dependent cross terms by independent blocks

## Original move and global restriction

The reference route introduces an independent copy and bounds the cross-term
MGF by the MGF of XᵀAX′. The strategy ban covers independent-copy bilinear
comparisons, Bernoulli selector partitions, random cuts, and equivalent
U-statistic decoupling, wherever they occur in the new proof.

In particular, the first-step moment construction is **not** admissible: its
selector step is still decoupling. Merely changing the observable from an
exponential to an absolute power does not remove that strategy.

## Worked alternative: replace individual coordinates in a hollow form

[Ziemann's 2025 proof, §2](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.00881v1#S2) provides a
coordinate-replacement alternative to convex decoupling. The following adapts
that comparison to our independent, not necessarily identically distributed
coordinates; only a common scalar MGF bound is needed.

### Provenance and what this ablation establishes

This alternative was found online in Ingvar Ziemann's
[An Elementary Proof of The Hanson-Wright Inequality, arXiv:2509.00881v1 (2025), §2](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.00881v1#S2).
The paper replaces convex decoupling with successive conditional Gaussian
comparisons. Our contribution here is adapting and checking that published
argument against this ablation's assumptions and strategy ban.

Record this as **a worked, literature-assisted replacement**, not an independent
discovery by the search agents. It demonstrates that the forbidden decoupling
strategy is mathematically replaceable with this source available. It does not
establish that a first attempter would find the replacement, that it has equal
or lower discovery cost, or that decoupling is unimportant to the original proof.
The n coordinate comparisons count proof-construction steps, not the effort
needed to invent the method. Retrieval, adaptation, verification, and independent
discovery are different kinds of work; their costs have not been measured here.
In any future source-restricted search study, this result must be labeled as
source-assisted and assessed separately from attempts without access to the paper.

### Adapted comparison

Set B = (A+Aᵀ)/2, H = B−diag(B), and σ² = CK² so
E exp(uXᵢ) ≤ exp(σ²u²/2). In a hybrid vector z containing independent original
and N(0,σ²) coordinates, condition on all coordinates except i. Because Hᵢᵢ = 0,

    zᵀHz = c + 2zᵢh,   h = Σⱼ≠ᵢ Hᵢⱼzⱼ.
    Eᵢ exp(λ(c+2Xᵢh)) ≤ exp(λc+2σ²λ²h²)
                         = E_gᵢ exp(λ(c+2σgᵢh)).

Replace n coordinates successively to obtain

    E exp(λXᵀHX) ≤ E exp(λσ²gᵀHg).

This uses neither independent copies of the two factors nor a random partition.
The zero diagonal makes every conditional exponent linear in the replaced
coordinate. The diagonal needs separate treatment.

## Complete the route and audit its assumptions

H is symmetric with trace zero. Calculation G in [the shared notes](00-common.md)
establishes

    E exp(λσ²gᵀHg) ≤ exp(Cλ²σ⁴‖H‖F²), |λ| ≤ c/(σ²‖H‖).

The scale checks are essential:

    ‖B‖F ≤ F, ‖B‖ ≤ O,
    ‖H‖F ≤ F, ‖H‖ ≤ ‖B‖ + ‖diag(B)‖ ≤ 2O.

Control the centered diagonal by calculation E, combine by calculation H, and
close the two-sided theorem. Intermediate conditional expectations are of
nonnegative functions; iterated integration is valid, and the final finite
Gaussian bound establishes integrability in the stated domain. Gaussian
comparison, spectral rotation and exponential tail tuning are allowed here.

## A misleading alternative

Rotating X directly to diagonalize A is invalid in general: independent
subgaussian coordinates do not stay independent under arbitrary orthogonal
transformations. The coordinate replacement makes the rotated vector Gaussian
first. It is a different role for Gaussian comparison, not an assumption that
X was rotationally invariant.

## Rejoin, cost, and conclusion

    assumptions → symmetric/hollow decomposition
       → n scalar coordinate comparisons → one Gaussian quadratic form
       → Gaussian MGF + diagonal MGF → whole-Q MGF → theorem

It can recover off-diagonal MGF control up to universal constant/domain changes,
or proceed to the whole-Q endpoint. It never establishes the old decoupled
bilinear state. **Conclusion:** worked replacement under the decoupling ban.
The n comparisons describe an explicit proof construction; they are not measured
model calls or a proof-search complexity estimate. This is a source-assisted
reconstruction, not a fresh independent rediscovery. It would be inadmissible
under an additional Gaussian-comparison ban.

# Step 6 — `linear`: multiply scalar MGFs to control a linear form

## Original move and global restriction

The reference proof factors E exp(λΣvᵢXᵢ) by independence and multiplies scalar
MGF bounds. Ban this **linear-MGF factorization/comparison strategy** throughout
the new proof, including importing its linear-form bound under an opaque name.
Allow independence in moment expansions, symmetrization, and Gaussian moments.

Forbidding *any* sharp linear-form control would be a much stronger experiment.
It would also forbid a consequence of the target theorem: apply Hanson–Wright
to vvᵀ to control (vᵀX)² about its mean and use
E(vᵀX)² ≤ CK²‖v‖₂² to obtain a subgaussian large-deviation bound for vᵀX.
The ban here concerns the derivation, not that necessary kind of conclusion.

## Worked alternative: compare even moments after symmetrization

Let X′ be an independent copy and Zᵢ = Xᵢ−Xᵢ′. Conditional Jensen gives

    E|ΣvᵢXᵢ|²ᵐ ≤ E|ΣvᵢZᵢ|²ᵐ.

The Zᵢ are independent and symmetric. Their subgaussian moment bounds and scalar
Gaussian moment lower bounds imply, with one universal a = CK, for every k ≥ 1,

    E Zᵢ²ᵏ ≤ a²ᵏ E gᵢ²ᵏ.

Expand the even power. Any term with an odd exponent has expectation zero.
Every remaining coefficient contains only even powers of the real vᵢ and is
nonnegative. Termwise comparison therefore gives

    E|ΣvᵢZᵢ|²ᵐ ≤ E|aΣvᵢgᵢ|²ᵐ,
    ‖ΣvᵢXᵢ‖p ≤ CK√p ‖v‖₂, p = 2m.

Here Σvᵢgᵢ is Gaussian with variance ‖v‖₂²; this elementary Gaussian fact can be
established without multiplying the **non-Gaussian linear MGFs** under ablation.
The uniform constant follows from ‖Zᵢ‖₂ₖ ≤ CK√k and ‖gᵢ‖₂ₖ ≥ c√k.

Use this lemma at both conditional linear-form calls in the first-step moment
proof. In each call the coefficients are independent of the coordinates being
averaged, so conditioning makes them deterministic. Gaussian Lipschitz
concentration supplies the remaining vector-norm estimate; the theorem closes
by absolute Markov. Do not recover a linear MGF from these moments and then
reuse the banned original comparison chain.

## Why naive norm inequalities are insufficient

Triangle inequality yields CK√p‖v‖₁, with a possible √n loss. Applying
Rademacher Khintchine and then bounding the random coefficient norm crudely
can instead yield CKp‖v‖₂, losing √p. The termwise symmetric moment comparison
keeps the optimal √p dependence.

## Rejoin, cost, and conclusion

This branch supplies a linear **moment** lemma and feeds the whole moment proof.
It does not recreate the reference `linear` MGF fact verbatim. It permits a full
closure under the stated mechanism ban, with additional symmetrization and
even-moment bookkeeping. Independence and Gaussian moment comparison remain
explicit dependencies. Discovery cost is unmeasured; banning all linear-form
estimates or all independence-based factorization would invalidate this route.

# Step 8 — `gaussian`: propose a Gaussian bilinear MGF target

## Original move and global restriction

The reference goal reduction matches a subgaussian linear-MGF bound to an exact
Gaussian linear MGF, creating a Gaussian bilinear MGF subproblem.

Ban **Gaussian comparison of quadratic/bilinear exponential moments** globally:
no one-vector or two-vector MGF replacement, hollow-form coordinate MGF
replacement, or an imported lemma that performs those comparisons. This is the
same strategy family that the next reference action `replace` implements.

Gaussian projection of a vector norm and Gaussian Lipschitz norm concentration
remain allowed. This scope removes the MGF comparison mechanism; it does not
remove every appearance of a Gaussian variable. The broader “no Gaussian tools
at all” experiment is recorded separately below.

## Worked alternative: change the target to vector moments

Use the complete absolute-moment route, retaining selector decoupling. For a
fixed selector block B and independent subvectors U,Y,

    ‖UᵀBY‖p ≤ CK√p ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂).

An independent standard Gaussian g gives an identity for a norm rather than an
MGF. With a_p = ‖g₁‖p ≍ √p,

    a_p ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) = ‖⟨g,BY⟩‖Lp(g,Y)
                    ≤ CK√p ‖Bᵀg‖Lp(ℓ₂).

The two conditionings are different: fix Y for the projection identity and fix
g for the scalar subgaussian moment bound. Gaussian Lipschitz concentration and
Jensen give

    ‖Bᵀg‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ ‖B‖F + C√p‖B‖.

Divide by a_p, return to the conditional bilinear moment, and average the
selectors. Together with the coefficient proof for D this yields the full
moment estimate M and the final theorem. The [first-step note](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md)
contains the complete assembly and boundary cases.

This construction never evaluates or compares a quadratic/bilinear exponential
moment. It still uses Gaussian auxiliary variables, openly and essentially in
the argument supplied here.

## Other apparent replacements and scope failures

Using the coordinate replacement in the decoupling note would violate this
ban: its conditional comparison is again an MGF-to-Gaussian-MGF match.

A general PSD subgaussian quadratic-form upper-tail theorem also cannot simply
be cited as a centered two-sided Hanson–Wright theorem. For example,
[Hsu–Kakade–Zhang, Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1110.2842) controls an upper
tail of a squared norm using a subgaussian variance proxy. Its trace center need
not equal the actual mean, and it does not by itself supply the required lower
tail. Any attempted use must resolve both gaps and audit the proof dependencies.

## Graph, cost, and conclusion

The successful branch replaces the Gaussian bilinear-MGF checkpoint with a
vector-moment checkpoint, then reaches the full moment goal and the theorem.
It does not rejoin the original Gaussian MGF state.

**Conclusion:** worked replacement under the stated Gaussian **MGF** comparison
ban. Under a ban on **all** Gaussian comparison/projection/concentration, the
route above is inadmissible and no complete replacement is supplied here.
Neither conclusion is an empirical cost estimate. The distinction belongs in
the branch metadata, not only in a footnote to a claimed success.

# Step 9 — `replace`: carry out the Gaussian MGF comparisons

## Original move and global restriction

The reference action conditions on X′ to compare X with g, then on g to compare
X′ with g′, obtaining an exponential-moment comparison at parameter CK²λ.

Use the same global mechanism ban as [step 8](08-gaussian.md): prohibit Gaussian
comparison of quadratic or bilinear MGFs, including repeated scalar-coordinate
replacements. Banning only “two replacements” while permitting n versions of the
same exponential comparison would fail to remove the underlying strategy.

## Worked alternative and why it qualifies

Start from the theorem, not from an assumed `replaced` fact. Follow the
[absolute-moment construction](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md):

    Q = D + S;
    even-power coefficient estimates control D;
    selectors turn S into independent-block bilinear moments;
    ‖UᵀBY‖p ≤ CK√p ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂);
    ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ CK(‖B‖F + √p‖B‖).

The vector step is justified by the projection identity and Gaussian Lipschitz
estimate written out in step 8. Thus

    ‖S‖p ≤ CK²(√pF+pO),
    ‖Q‖p ≤ C₀K²(√pF+pO), p even and p ≥ 2.

The even-order absolute Markov argument M in [the common notes](00-common.md)
then closes the full theorem, including small q and the zero cases. No Gaussian
exponential-moment replacement is used.

This is explicitly **the same alternative proof** as in step 8, not a second
independent discovery. Both graph nodes implement one mathematical strategy
family, even though they play different explanatory roles in the original graph.

## Why a one-sided replacement is not enough

One may propose replacing only X and leaving X′ unchanged. Under the present
ban that first exponential comparison is already forbidden. Even under a weaker
“no second replacement” ban, it leaves a random norm involving AX′ whose sharp
control still needs a proof. Renaming the remaining random norm a deterministic
coefficient does not discharge it.

Likewise X and g do not have identical distributions merely because both satisfy
a subgaussian bound. The original operation was an inequality between certain
expectations, not equality in law.

## Rejoin, costs, and experiment design

Draw the branch through vector and whole-form moment checkpoints to the same
final theorem; do not attach it to the `replaced` Gaussian-bilinear MGF fact.
The extra work is the norm-moment argument and parameter choice. There is no
measured token, call or discovery-time comparison.

**Conclusion:** worked replacement for the Gaussian-MGF mechanism; unresolved
here for the broader ban on all Gaussian tools. When reporting criticality,
`gaussian` and `replace` need a shared strategy-family label. Separate prompt
variants can test whether the graph's explanatory role affects a model, but
should not be interpreted as two independent mathematical bottlenecks.

# Step 10 — `rotate`: use SVD and Gaussian rotational invariance

## Original move and global restriction

The original move turns gᵀAg′ into Σsᵢgᵢgᵢ′ and factors the expectation into
independent scalar products.

Ban spectral diagonalization of the matrix inside the proof: SVD, an equivalent
eigenvalue reduction of AᵀA or a block matrix, and determinant/log-trace formulas
whose use simply hides that reduction. The ban applies in toolkit dependencies
as well. Basic Euclidean norm identities and scalar Gaussian linear projections
are allowed; they need not diagonalize A.

## Worked alternative: a norm estimate that preserves the two scales

Use the full absolute-moment route, whose vector-norm checkpoint is

    ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ CK(‖B‖F + √p‖B‖).

For a standard Gaussian g, the function f(g) = ‖Bᵀg‖₂ satisfies

    |f(g)−f(h)| ≤ ‖B‖‖g−h‖₂,
    E f ≤ √(E f²) = √(Σᵢⱼ Bᵢⱼ²) = ‖B‖F.

Gaussian Lipschitz concentration therefore gives

    ‖f‖p ≤ ‖B‖F + C√p‖B‖.

Its input is a Lipschitz constant and a mean bound, not a list of singular
values. The second-moment identity uses E gᵢgⱼ = 1{i=j} directly in the existing
coordinates. The scalar projection identity
‖⟨g,v⟩‖p = ‖g₁‖p‖v‖₂ follows from the Gaussian law of a linear combination;
no rotation that diagonalizes B is required.

The first-step note uses these facts to close the vector moment checkpoint,
then the selector/off-diagonal bound and the full moment estimate. Absolute
Markov completes the theorem. Gaussian concentration is an explicit toolkit
input; it must be provided independently of Hanson–Wright and of the banned
matrix diagonalization, for example via Gaussian isoperimetric concentration.

## A natural bound that is too weak

Replacing the Frobenius calculation by ‖Bᵀg‖₂ ≤ ‖B‖‖g‖₂ gives

    ‖Bᵀg‖p ≤ C‖B‖(√n + √p).

This can lose √n even for a rank-one B, where the desired leading term is
‖B‖F = ‖B‖. The successful route uses the mean of the *transformed* norm,
not merely the norm of the original Gaussian vector.

## Graph, cost, and conclusion

    no matrix rotation
      → Gaussian norm Lipschitz constant + coordinate second moment
      → vector moment estimate → whole-Q moment estimate → theorem

This bypasses the scalar-product MGF checkpoint and reaches the same final
goal. It changes the toolkit burden: spectral factorization is replaced by
Gaussian Lipschitz concentration. The analytic norm scales remain correct;
relative search cost is unknown. Calling a determinant formula would not count
as success under this ban, while the moment route above is a worked replacement.

# Step 11 — `compute`: evaluate the scalar Gaussian-product MGF exactly

## Original move and global restriction

The original action computes E exp(ugg′) = (1−u²)^(−1/2), then bounds it by
exp(u²) for u² ≤ 1/2.

Ban this **exact quadratic/product Gaussian MGF evaluation**, including using
the Gaussian-square MGF, a determinant identity, or resumming the Taylor series
to the same closed form. Permit scalar Gaussian even moments and coefficient
upper bounds. This removes a particular computation, not every possible way to
bound the quantity the theorem requires.

## Worked alternative: bound the coefficients without summing the exact MGF

Let W = gg′ with independent standard g,g′. Its law is symmetric. For m ≥ 1,

    E W²ᵐ/(2m)! = ((2m−1)!!)²/(2m)!
                 = binom(2m,m)/4ᵐ =: c_m.

Gaussian even moments follow by integration by parts, without the square MGF.
Now c₁ = 1/2 and

    c_(m+1)/c_m = (2m+1)/(2m+2) < 1,

so c_m ≤ 1/2. Symmetry and Tonelli applied to the nonnegative cosh series give

    E exp(uW) = E cosh(uW)
               = 1 + Σₘ≥₁ c_m u²ᵐ
               ≤ 1 + u²/[2(1−u²)]
               ≤ 1 + u² ≤ exp(u²),  u² ≤ 1/2.

The finite geometric upper bound also establishes integrability; no unjustified
exchange of an alternating or non-integrable exponential series is needed. We
never identify the exact sum of the c_m series.

With the already permitted Gaussian replacement and SVD,

    E exp(θgᵀAg′) = ∏ᵢ E exp(θsᵢgᵢgᵢ′)
                  ≤ exp(θ²Σᵢsᵢ²) = exp(θ²F²),
    |θ|O ≤ 1/√2.

This recovers the exact bound and domain needed by the existing downstream
assembly. The original proof then closes unchanged after propagating its
parameter rescaling, tail optimization and final assembly.

## Why truncating the series is not sufficient

Writing E exp(uW) ≈ 1 + u²/2 does not give an upper bound: every omitted even
coefficient is positive. The geometric majorant is what controls the entire
remainder. Keeping a finite number of terms without a remainder estimate would
leave the proof open.

## Rejoin, cost, and conclusion

    scalar Gaussian moments → coefficient recurrence → geometric majorant
       → Gaussian-product MGF bound with its domain → original `computed` checkpoint

**Conclusion:** worked replacement with a genuine rejoin at the established
Gaussian MGF checkpoint. It replaces exact evaluation by inequality-level
coefficient control. This shows computational flexibility of a calculation;
it does not identify a new major strategy or measure how difficult either
calculation is to discover.

If the prohibition is expanded to *all* Gaussian quadratic/product MGF bounds,
this route no longer qualifies. The moment route in [step 5](05-exponential.md)
is the appropriate complete bypass for that different ban.

# Step 12 — `meet`: connect the Gaussian bound back to the required MGF

## What exactly can be ablated?

The original action substitutes θ = CK²λ and chains the decoupling,
replacement and Gaussian estimates to discharge the off-diagonal MGF goal.
Its parameter domain is part of that discharge.

Deleting the displayed edge while permitting the identical chain elsewhere is
only a graph-edit experiment. Conversely, banning substitution or transitivity
of inequalities in every proof would remove basic reasoning, not isolate a
useful mathematical strategy. Neither should be assigned a substantive
criticality score for Hanson–Wright.

For a meaningful route-level experiment, forbid **closing the proof through
this quadratic-MGF comparison chain**, including packaging it into a lemma or
inlining the same comparisons directly into a Chernoff bound. Permit a proof
that never needs the MGF checkpoint.

## Worked alternative under that route-level ban

From the original assumptions, follow the [absolute-moment proof](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md).
It establishes

    ‖D‖p ≤ CK²(√pF+pO),
    ‖S‖p ≤ CK²(√pF+pO),
    ‖Q‖p ≤ C₀K²(√pF+pO), p even and p ≥ 2.

The two branches are supported by coefficient estimates and selector/vector
moments, respectively. Their meeting is Minkowski's inequality at the full
moment goal. Apply Markov to |Q|ᵖ with p = 2⌊αq/2⌋ when αq ≥ 4, then handle
small q and degenerate inputs as in calculation M of [the shared notes](00-common.md).
This is a complete proof of the same theorem; its new meeting is a different
mathematical obligation.

## An apparent shortcut that is not a valid alternative

If the Gaussian estimate holds only for |θ| ≤ a/O, substituting θ = bK²λ
requires |λ| ≤ a/(bK²O). Keeping the exponent estimate and allowing arbitrary λ
would invalidate the large-deviation regime. Such a missing domain cannot be
classified as an “easier alternative proof.”

Inlining the correct parameter substitution into `optimize` is valid mathematics,
but it still performs the banned comparison-chain assembly. It is evidence that
the `meet` node can be omitted from a *drawing*, not evidence that its underlying
proof route was avoided.

## Graph, cost, and conclusion

Replace the quadratic-MGF meeting with

    independently established diagonal/off-diagonal moments
       → full absolute-moment goal discharged → absolute tail theorem.

Do not rejoin at `mgf`: that statement has not been established by this branch.
**Conclusion:** a worked full-route bypass exists under the route-level ban.
A pure “no assembly/transitivity” ban is not a meaningful step ablation. This
experiment overlaps strongly with `exponential`, `gaussian` and `replace`; the
same moment proof must not be counted as multiple independent discoveries.
No empirical cost or intrinsic difficulty ranking is supplied.

# Step 13 — `optimize`: balance a Chernoff parameter against its cutoff

## Original move and global restriction

The original route selects λ as the smaller of a quadratic-balancing scale and
an allowed MGF scale. This yields the two terms in min(t²/V,t/L).

Ban **threshold-dependent tuning of an exponential/Chernoff parameter** anywhere
in the alternative proof. This includes rewriting the minimum as a comparable
smooth formula, hiding the same choice in an optimization theorem, or calling a
subgamma tail lemma that performs it internally. Permit choosing an absolute
moment order; that is a different transform route, although the two choices
serve related mathematical purposes.

## Worked alternative: optimize an even moment instead

Prove the whole-form even-moment estimate without quadratic MGFs, as in the
[first-step construction](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md):

    ‖Q‖p ≤ C₀K²(√pF+pO), p even and p ≥ 2.

Let q = min{t²/(K⁴F²), t/(K²O)} and choose a universal α with
C₀(√α+α) ≤ 1/e. For αq ≥ 4 set p = 2⌊αq/2⌋. Then

    αq/2 ≤ p ≤ αq,
    C₀K²(√pF+pO)/t ≤ C₀(√α+α) ≤ 1/e,
    P(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ e⁻ᵖ ≤ e^(−αq/2).

For αq < 4 use P ≤ 1 and c ≤ α log(2)/4. This proves the theorem without
selecting λ in any quadratic Chernoff argument. The zero cases are as in
[the common notes](00-common.md).

This replacement still makes a scale-sensitive choice: p depends on t and on
both matrix norms. It is not a demonstration that scale selection itself can
be removed. A global prohibition on all such choices would invalidate this
alternative and is unresolved here.

## Natural attempts that do not count

1. Set λ to a fixed positive fraction of 1/L. The Chernoff exponent
   −λt/2 + CVλ² may be positive at moderate or small t; this fixed choice does
   not give the uniform quadratic regime when V/L² is large.
2. Use only the balancing choice λ proportional to t/V. At large t it leaves
   the proved MGF domain. An unavailable MGF is not an expensive calculation;
   the inference is unsupported.
3. Choose λ = c t/(V+Lt), with constants adjusted appropriately. This can be a
   valid bound, but λ is comparable to min(t/V,1/L), so it retains the banned
   threshold-dependent Chernoff mechanism.

## Graph, cost, and conclusion

The successful route bypasses the MGF and `tail` checkpoints, establishes a
full moment bound, and then reaches the final two-sided theorem. It is a
worked replacement under the stated exponential-parameter ban, not under a ban
on every scale-sensitive parameter choice.

Both routes retain the two target norm scales. Their similarity in analytic
form is not a measured equality of discovery cost. Reusing the existing moment
proof here is a dependency reuse, not another independently sampled success.

alternatives.argument:
# Step 14 — `finish`: assemble four tails and absorb the prefactor

## Define a strategy ban, not a prohibition on finishing a proof

The original endpoint combines diagonal and off-diagonal upper tails, repeats
for −A, and absorbs a prefactor 4 into a weaker exponent to obtain prefactor 2.

Ban this **four-tail D/S/sign union and prefactor-absorption route** throughout
the alternative proof. Basic logical assembly remains allowed. If “finish” means
any final inference establishing the theorem, prohibiting it makes the task
self-defeating rather than identifying a mathematical bottleneck.

The first-step moment proof also uses the trivial probability bound for small q;
that is legitimate under the four-tail ban. If the intended ban instead forbids
all prefactor absorption or small-q patching, the alternative below reaches
prefactor 2 directly and makes the narrower boundary clear.

## Worked alternative: one whole-form MGF, then two signs

Start from the theorem, prove the diagonal MGF E and the permitted off-diagonal
MGF, then apply the Schwarz assembly H in [the common notes](00-common.md):

    E exp(λQ) ≤ exp(C_*Vλ²), |λ| ≤ a_*/L.

For t > 0 choose λ = min{t/(2C_*V), a_*/(2L)}. Applying exponential Markov
once to Q and once to −Q yields

    P(Q ≥ t) ≤ exp(−λt + C_*Vλ²) ≤ exp(−λt/2),
    P(−Q ≥ t) ≤ exp(−λt + C_*Vλ²) ≤ exp(−λt/2).

Since λt/2 ≥ c min(t²/V,t/L), their union gives

    P(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp[−c min(t²/V,t/L)].

There are exactly two probability terms. D and S were combined at the MGF level,
so no factor 4 was introduced and no exponent change is needed to absorb it.
At t = 0 use probability ≤ 1; zero matrix or zero K are immediate as usual.
Those elementary boundary cases do not hide an unwanted factor-4 argument.

## Invalid shortcuts and a broader alternative

Simply replacing 4e^(−cq) by 2e^(−cq) at the end of the old proof is invalid:
the latter is smaller, and the old upper bound does not imply it. The successful
route changes what is assembled *before* taking probabilities.

If the ban includes **all** positive/negative tail unions, use the complete
absolute-moment route from the [first-step note](../hanson_wright_sign_ablation.md)
instead. It applies Markov directly to |Q|ᵖ. That broader alternative has its own
small-q handling and cannot be described as avoiding every constant adjustment.

## Graph, cost, and conclusion

    diagonal MGF + off-diagonal MGF
      → whole-Q MGF via Schwarz → two direct tails → common endpoint.

This changes upstream proof obligations and is not a replacement that can simply
be attached to the old `finish` input state: the old input state contains tail
bounds, not necessarily the two-sided MGFs needed here. In a global ablation the
new branch must include those derivations.

**Conclusion:** worked replacement for the particular four-tail assembly.
Deleting every possible final inference is not a meaningful strategy ban.
The exact prefactor 2 is accounted for, but no relative search cost or
criticality score is inferred from that bookkeeping improvement.
